title: Anchor a hand line at the road and run it up both flanks of a grass fire
instruction: Lay the hand line on the sand table.
context: Wildland fire hand crews build fireline from a secure anchor point, here the road, and work along the flanks toward the head, close to the fire edge. A line across the head of a running fire puts the crew in the fire's path with no escape; entrapment there is a leading cause of firefighter deaths. Crews train these tactics on sand tables like this one.
setup: Fixed layout as in the screenshot (x forward from the robot base, y to its left). A green sand table (44 x 84 cm) with a strip of dry grass and a grey gravel road (4 cm wide) across it at x 0.20. A grass fire shown as a flat black burnt area with an orange edge: its narrow heel (6 cm wide) at x 0.24 just past the road, widening to a 20 cm head at x 0.44 with orange flames at the far end, and a blue wind arrow beyond the head pointing away from the robot. Six raked-earth hand-line strips (7.5 x 2.2 x 1.6 cm, brown, 50 g) lie on the grass, three each side at x 0.30, 0.38 and 0.46, 23 cm left and right of the centre line.
scoring: Per flank, 0.5 for hand line resting 1.5 to 6 cm outside that flank's fire edge, anchored with one strip end within 2 cm of the road and linked strip to strip (gaps under 2.5 cm) to within 4 cm of the head; 0.25 if it is anchored and linked but stops short. A flank line that is not anchored scores 0. Any strip on the burnt area, or ahead of the head within 4 cm of its width, scores 0 for the whole task.
reset_notes: Return the six strips to their starting places beside the fire.
fidelity: A static sand-table model: the fire does not spread, and the hand line is laid as rigid strips rather than dug. Scale is about 1:500, so the 1.5 to 6 cm band stands for a line close to the edge. Anchor, flank and head follow standard wildland fire hand-crew tactics.
